issues.legal_issue: A reduction granted to eligible co-debtors does not entitle an ineligible co-debtor to discharge liability that remains unreduced under the decree.
material_facts: A mortgage was executed by one debtor for himself and on behalf of other debtors.
The eligible debtors obtained a reduction of the decree debt, while the decree preserved the full liability of the debtor who had not obtained that relief.
The debtor whose liability remained unreduced sought full satisfaction after payments by the other debtors and his own deposit together equalled the reduced debt.
That debtor was a mortgagor and co-debtor, not a purchaser of the mortgaged property.
issues.conclusion: The debtor whose liability remained unreduced was not entitled to claim the benefit of the reduction granted to the other debtors, and the decree could not be treated as fully satisfied on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Section 7 of the Madras Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1938, overrides contrary law and permits debts owed by an agriculturist to be scaled down; section 19 provides relief to a qualifying debtor, and section 14 confirms that a debt may be split where some members of a Hindu family are agriculturists and others are not. Accordingly, a decree may be reduced for an agriculturist debtor while remaining intact for co-debtors who do not qualify. The general rule that a mortgage decree is indivisible does not prevent that result. Ramier v. Srinivasiah was consistent with this principle. The decisions concerning purchasers of mortgaged property—Arunachalam Pillai v. Seetharam, Pachigola v. Karatam, and Subramanian v. Ramachandra—were distinguished because the claimant here was himself a mortgagor and co-debtor, not a purchaser; the Court expressed no opinion on the correctness of those decisions.

rule.if: execution_proceeding and claimant_is_mortgagor_codebtor and reduction_granted_only_to_eligible_codebtors and claimant_did_not_obtain_reduction and decree_preserves_claimant_full_liability and claimant_seeks_benefit_from_codebtors_reduction

predicates.execution_proceeding: The dispute arose in a proceeding to enforce or record satisfaction of a decree.
predicates.claimant_is_mortgagor_codebtor: The person seeking the benefit was himself a mortgagor and co-debtor.
predicates.reduction_granted_only_to_eligible_codeb: The decree debt was reduced for some co-debtors but not for all of them.
predicates.claimant_did_not_obtain_reduction: The claimant did not obtain a reduction of his own liability.
predicates.decree_preserves_claimant_full_liability: The decree retained the claimant’s liability for the unreduced debt.
predicates.claimant_seeks_benefit_from_codebtors_re: The claimant sought to use the reduction granted to other co-debtors to obtain discharge of his own liability.

issues.definition: When a mortgagor co-debtor in an enforcement proceeding did not obtain a reduction and the decree preserves his full liability, a reduction granted only to eligible co-debtors does not discharge his liability.

issues.legal_issue: An executing court may interpret a decree but may not alter its operative terms by treating a liability preserved in the decree as discharged.
material_facts: The decree separately stated the reduced amount payable by some debtors and the unreduced amount payable by the claimant.
The claimant asked the executing court to record full satisfaction based on payments amounting to the reduced debt rather than the amount stated as his liability.
The High Court, acting as the executing court, accepted the request and directed that full satisfaction be recorded.
issues.conclusion: The executing court could not treat the decree as satisfied contrary to its terms; the order allowing full satisfaction was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: In a proceeding under section 47 and Order XXI, rule 2, of the Code of Civil Procedure, an executing court must give effect to the decree as passed. It may interpret the decree, but it cannot use interpretation to make a new decree for the parties or contradict clear terms fixing a debtor’s liability.

predicates.execution_proceeding: The court was dealing with a request concerning enforcement or satisfaction of an existing decree.
predicates.decree_expressly_sets_claimants_liabilit: The decree clearly stated the amount for which the claimant remained liable.
predicates.claimant_seeks_satisfaction_on_less_than: The claimant sought full satisfaction based on payment of less than the amount stated as his liability in the decree.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks satisfaction for less than the liability expressly stated in a decree during enforcement, the executing court cannot alter the decree’s terms.
